subject: Delivery gates & acceptance milestones for private-offer (Orchid Health)
messages:
From: Marianne Cole <marianne.cole@orchidhealth.com>

Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@orchidhealth.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Delivery gates and acceptance milestones for Redwood private offer (Orchid Health)

Hi Jonas / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement at Orchid needs a mutually agreed plan so our finance and platform teams can line up PO issuance and AWS private-offer activation. Attached is our procurement checklist for reference (high level).

High-level asks from our side:
- Confirm the sequence: PO -> Private Offer activation in AWS -> Acceptance window -> Invoice routing (AWS marketplace vs. direct invoicing).
- Clear acceptance gates (what counts as "Tech Accept") and test owners.
- Billing contacts and expected invoice cadence so our AP team can set vendor onboarding.

Tentative internal timeline:
- Week of May 6: PO issued (we expect legal signoff by then)
- Week of May 13: Private-offer activation / entitlement mapping
- Week of May 20: Completion of technical acceptance tests

Can you propose a MAP with checkpoints and owners? Also need to know if Redwood can accept invoice via AWS Marketplace (preferred) or whether you require direct billing.

I attached Orchid_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx.

Cheers,
Marianne Cole
Head of Procurement, Orchid Health
marianne.cole@orchidhealth.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Date: Fri, 03 May 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delivery gates and acceptance milestones for Redwood private offer (Orchid Health)

Hi Marianne — great to hear from you and thanks for the checklist. I put together a short MAP PDF (attached) that maps the procurement steps to product acceptance and billing events. Key notes up front:

- Redwood supports AWS Private Offer activation and can accept invoices through AWS Marketplace. That is typically the quickest path to entitlement and removes manual AP handoffs.
- We recommend a 7-business-day technical acceptance window after entitlement mapping for the eval tests you care about (see Aditya's test plan coming next).
- Billing: Marketplace invoice will be generated on activation and paid via your AP. If Orchid needs direct invoicing instead, we can do that but it will add ~2 business days to the activation cadence for our finance to reconcile.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Kickoff & PO alignment (owner: Marianne / Orchid Procurement) — target: by 2029-05-10
2) Private Offer activation (owner: AWS Marketplace + Redwood) — target: by 2029-05-13
3) Entitlement mapping + SSO & IAM checks (owner: Aditya / Orchid infra) — target: 2029-05-14 to 05-16
4) Technical acceptance tests (owner: Orchid QA + Aditya) — target: 7 business days from mapping
5) Final acceptance & Go-live (owner: Laura / Customer Success) — target: 2029-05-24

Next steps:
- Aditya, can you add the acceptance criteria and a short test checklist?
- Marianne, if you confirm Marketplace invoicing is preferred, we will proceed with that route — we will also share the DocuSign for the private-offer terms once legal confirms.

Attaching: RDW_MAP_v1.pdf

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Delivery gates and acceptance milestones for Redwood private offer (Orchid Health)

Thanks Jonas. Marianne — quick technical addendum with the acceptance plan. I broke this into three deliverables (we keep it tight to avoid scope creep):

Acceptance criteria (must pass all):
- Entitlements: Orchid accounts mapped to private-offer SKUs and test entitlements validated by Redwood admin console.
- SSO/SCIM: OKTA provisioning test — user in test group can reach the private offer and receive tokens.
- Model smoke tests: 10 representative prompt templates, throughput sanity (tail latency < 500ms p50 on test env), token accounting matches quota.
- Data handling: Confirm retention setting = 30 days (or customer-provided) and audit logging enabled.

Test owners and method:
- Entitlement mapping: Redwood (Aditya) will validate and provide screenshots + entitlement report.
- SSO provisioning: Orchid infra (Samir) + Redwood (Aditya) will run provisioning checklist.
- Model tests: Orchid QA will run prompts (we provide runbook). Redwood provides a test harness (script + tokens) and will be available for 2 hours during the first run.

I attached a short file with the acceptance test steps: acceptance_test_plan.md. If you want, we can run the first test together on 2029-05-15 morning — Jonas / Laura, does that work?

Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Delivery gates and acceptance milestones for Redwood private offer (Orchid Health)

Jonas / Aditya — quick update from our side after legal reviewed: two items

1) We attached our redlines related to liability and data retention. Legal would like a 90-day cure period on operational incidents and explicit data deletion SLA. See Orchid_Redlines_20290503.pdf.
2) Billing: Procurement prefers Marketplace invoicing, but legal wants to confirm that the invoice issued by AWS will include Redwood as the vendor name and that the PO reference will be clearly visible. Will AWS marketplace invoices contain our PO number in the line item?

If Redwood can confirm both (we think the Marketplace path is still preferred), we can issue the PO by EOD Wednesday (May 8). Otherwise procurement will ask for a direct invoice flow.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Platform Engineering | Orchid Health

Hi Marianne / Samir — thanks for the redlines and the billing question. Quick answers and commitment checkpoints below.

Billing & PO reference:
- AWS Marketplace invoices include the seller (Redwood Inference) and a reference field that can surface the PO number. We will work with AWS Marketplace Ops to ensure the PO number appears on the invoice line item. Ben (cc'd) will own the AWS ops coordination.
- If for any reason Marketplace invoicing cannot expose the PO in the exact format your AP system requires, we will offer a direct invoice fallback. That fallback is expected to add ~48 hours to activation while finance reconciles.

On the redlines: we reviewed the PDF. Our legal team is generally comfortable with a 60-day operational cure, but we will escalate the 90-day request to legal for a quick review and come back by EOD Tuesday. We can also accept a 30-day data deletion SLA with an optional addendum — Aditya will confirm technical feasibility for 30 vs 90 days.

Final MAP with checkpoints (dates updated):
- PO issued by Orchid (owner: Marianne) — target: 2029-05-08
- Private Offer activation by AWS + Redwood (owner: Ben / AWS Ops) — target: 2029-05-13
- Entitlement & SSO mapping (owner: Aditya / Samir) — target: 2029-05-14
- Technical acceptance tests (owner: Orchid QA + Redwood) — test window: 2029-05-15 to 2029-05-23 (7 business days)
- Final acceptance sign-off & go-live (owner: Laura) — target: 2029-05-24

Action items:
- Marianne: confirm PO path (Marketplace preferred) by EOD Wed (2029-05-08).
- Ben: coordinate with AWS Marketplace ops to validate PO-on-invoice capability and link us to the AWS contact.
- Aditya: confirm data deletion SLA options by tomorrow.
- Jonas / Laura: prepare the DocuSign for private-offer terms once legal confirms.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth activation.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
